verdicts.flaw_description: In two of the four blocks the measured gain predates the intervention: Hollow Ridge was 'fitted 3 August' but the 0.6 t/ha gain is recorded 'by 18 June', and Bellamy Flats was 'fitted 2 May' but the 0.7 t/ha gain is recorded 'by 17 March'. The other two blocks (fitted 8 December / by 23 February; fitted 7 September / by 22 November) run forward on a consistent ~2.5 month lag, so cases One and Three have measurement dates falling before the drip line existed.

A named alternative cause reaches every plot: 'Prey abundance on the surrounding farmland doubled from the previous year, and every box stood at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range.' Since the comparison is to the previous spring, doubled food supply within foraging range can fully account for the 9-16 extra fledglings without the boxes contributing anything.

Two of the four classes have outcome dates that precede the start of the program: Ashcombe 'started the program 6 December' but scored higher 'by 11 September', and Halloway 'started the program 20 June' but scored higher 'by 24 April'. The other two (8 January / by 12 March; 6 July / by 21 August) run forward on short lags, so the gains in cases One and Three were measured before the program began.

The numbers cover a narrower population than the claim: 'Pass rates cover the students entered for the exam, and about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered', with no rule filling in the non-entered students. Withholding the weakest quarter of each roll from entry raises the pass rate mechanically, so the 4-8 point gains need not reflect any improvement in the cohorts the tutoring blocks were given to.
